name: Prepare and run board and committee meetings
summary: The board secretariat prepares and runs about 27 board and committee meetings a year: the board, finance and audit, human resources and compensation, nominating and governance and, from September 2021, a board investment committee of all directors. For each meeting the secretary agrees the agenda with the chief executive, general counsel and chair, collects papers from executive sponsors, checks them, publishes a book in the board portal at least a week ahead, records decisions and conflicts at the meeting, and turns notes into minutes that the chair reviews and the next meeting approves. Most elapsed time is waiting: on executives' and the chair's calendars, on paper drafting that depends on other processes closing, and on directors' reading time. Late, long papers and rework after review are the common problems.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager of about 240 staff that invests about $79 billion for a few public pension plans and an insurance board through pooled funds and segregated accounts, on a cost recovery basis.
baseline.notes: Nine directors in 2021 and a two-person secretariat reporting to the general counsel and corporate secretary. Paper content comes from other processes (financial statements, risk reports, performance results, budget, audits, investment decisions); this workflow covers the meeting cycle around them. The annual members' meeting is a separate process.

trigger: A meeting falls due in the annual board and committee work plan, or the chair or chief executive calls a special meeting for an urgent decision.
end_state: The meeting has been held, draft minutes have been reviewed by the chair, decisions and actions have been sent to their owners and the records are filed; formal approval of the minutes happens at the next meeting.

volume.seasonality: Busier from February to April (financial statements, annual report, year-end performance and compensation) and from October to December (budget, investment plan and benchmarks, strategic plan); lighter in July and August. Special meetings cluster in market stress, as in spring 2020.

evidence.note: 27 meetings in 2020 (11 board, 6 finance and audit, 5 human resources and compensation, 5 nominating and governance), 28 in 2021 (10, 6, 6, 4 and 2 Board Investment Committee) and 27 in 2022 (5 board, 7 Board Investment Committee, 6, 4, 5): about 2.3 a month. The organisation file's mode of 2 is slightly low.

Cost range copied from the organisation file (Job Bank Toronto wages deflated to 2021 plus variable pay, times a 1.35 loading; executives priced from reported pay). FTE: about 20 to 25 hours of agenda, paper review, meeting and minutes work per meeting at 2.3 meetings a month, plus governance records, policies register and the members' meeting outside this process (author estimate).

systems.name: Document management system and virtual data rooms
Email, video calls and collaboration suite

steps.name: Open the meeting file from the annual work plan
steps.description: The governance coordinator opens the board or committee annual work plan, lists the items the mandate requires at this meeting (standing reports, annual approvals, prior minutes, the action log), creates the meeting folder in the document system and an empty book in the board portal, and confirms the date with directors. A short-notice special meeting called for a large investment or an urgent matter goes down a shorter path.
inputs: annual board and committee work plan

error.defect_description: A mandated annual item, such as a charter review or policy renewal, is left off the list.

evidence.note: Meeting counts (27, 28 and 27 board and committee meetings in 2020 to 2022) and committee mandates are stated; the work plan practice and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Draft the agenda
steps.description: The board secretary drafts the agenda: standing items, decisions management wants, items carried forward from the action log and the work plan, with time allotted to each and a split between items for decision and items for information. Prior minutes for approval go on the agenda.

error.defect_description: Time allotted is unrealistic or a decision item is missing.

evidence.note: Agenda prioritises actionable items with time allotted; times are author estimates.

steps.name: CEO and general counsel review the agenda
steps.description: In a short agenda meeting the chief executive and the general counsel, who is also corporate secretary, go through the draft agenda with the secretary, add or drop management items and agree who presents each paper.

control.basis: Board and committee mandates: agenda prepared by the corporate secretary with the CEO for the chair

evidence.note: Common practice; executive calendars make this the first queue. Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Chair approves the agenda
steps.description: The secretary sends the agenda to the board or committee chair, often with a call, and the chair approves it or adds items. The approved agenda fixes which papers are needed.

control.basis: Committee mandates: the chair is responsible for the agenda

evidence.note: The chair owns the agenda with staff support; wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Issue the call for papers
steps.description: The coordinator emails the executive sponsors and authors the approved agenda, the paper template (purpose, decision sought, recommendation, risks, executive summary), the paper deadline about two weeks before the meeting and the list of standing reports due from risk, finance, audit and compliance, and starts a paper tracker.

error.defect_description: An author is missed or given the wrong deadline.

evidence.note: Executive summaries and focused content recommended; deadline is an author estimate.

steps.name: Executive sponsors prepare and approve their papers
steps.description: The sponsoring executives (chief financial officer, chief risk officer, chief investment officer, head of HR) and their teams turn the outputs of other processes, such as financial statements, risk reports, performance results, the budget, audit reports and investment decisions, into board papers with cover memos and recommendations, and approve them. Papers often run long or arrive late because source data closes late.

error.defect_description: A paper is too long, lacks a clear decision request, or has numbers that differ from another paper.

evidence.note: Directors report packs of 200 to more than 950 pages and quality concerns; sponsor time per meeting is an author estimate.

steps.name: Chase late and missing papers
steps.description: After the deadline the coordinator checks the tracker, emails and phones the authors of late papers, agrees new times and warns the secretary which items may have to be tabled late or deferred.

evidence.note: Late materials are a common director complaint; share of meetings with late papers is an author estimate.

steps.name: Secretary reviews the papers
steps.description: The secretary reads every paper against the template: is the decision sought clear, is there an executive summary, is it a reasonable length, is it consistent with earlier minutes and resolutions, and is the draft resolution worded correctly. Papers that fall short go back to the sponsor with comments.

error.defect_description: An inconsistency between papers is missed.

control.basis: Board paper guidelines (template, length, decision request)

evidence.note: Quality checks follow published guidance on board materials; rework share is an author estimate.

steps.name: General counsel reviews resolutions and legal items
steps.description: The general counsel reviews draft resolutions, delegations of authority and any paper with legal or regulatory effect, such as pool trust amendments, by-law changes or policy approvals, and flags items where a director may have a conflict of interest.

error.defect_description: Resolution wording does not match the authority needed.

control.basis: Corporate secretary review of resolutions under the by-laws and delegation of authority

next.condition: decision papers on investments, policies or plans

evidence.note: Typical corporate secretary practice; shares and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Chief risk officer adds risk commentary to decision papers
steps.description: For board and investment committee meetings with decisions on investments, policies, plans or benchmarks, the chief risk officer reviews the papers and adds or confirms the independent risk view that directors expect beside management's recommendation.

control.basis: Risk management framework: independent risk view on decision papers

evidence.note: Independent risk review and board risk oversight are described; frequency is an author estimate.

steps.name: CEO signs off the pack
steps.description: The chief executive reads the near-final papers, checks that key messages are consistent and that management's recommendation is clear, and signs off or asks for changes to particular papers.

control.basis: Management accountability for board papers: CEO sign-off

evidence.note: Common practice; times and rework share are author estimates.

steps.name: Assemble the board book in the portal
steps.description: The coordinator converts the final papers to PDF, builds the book in the portal in agenda order with the draft prior minutes and action log, adds bookmarks and a reading room for background material, and sets permissions so in-camera and committee-only items are visible only to the right people.

error.defect_description: A superseded version is loaded or a permission is wrong.

evidence.note: Portal book building and permissions follow vendor documentation; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Proof and publish the book
steps.description: The secretary previews the book as a director would see it, checks versions, page order and permissions, publishes it and emails directors that it is available, aiming for at least a week before the meeting.

error.defect_description: A page or attachment is missing in the published book.

control.basis: Paper distribution standard: materials at least one week before the meeting

next.condition: late paper or addendum to follow

evidence.note: One-week distribution is the published best-practice standard; the share of meetings with late additions is an author estimate.

steps.name: Add late papers and republish
steps.description: When a late paper or an addendum arrives, the coordinator loads it, has the secretary check it, republishes the book and emails directors a note on what changed. Directors then have less time to read it.

evidence.note: Republishing after edits is vendor practice; late arrival is a common complaint.

steps.name: Directors read the pack
steps.description: Directors read the book in the portal, annotate it and send questions to the secretary or chair. The meeting date is fixed by the calendar, so this wait does not shrink if the pack is early.

evidence.note: At least a week of reading time is recommended.

steps.name: Arrange logistics and confirm quorum
steps.description: The executive assistant books the room and video link, confirms attendance against quorum, schedules presenters' time slots, arranges directors' travel and meals and processes their expense claims and meeting fee records.

error.defect_description: Quorum or a presenter is not confirmed in time.

control.basis: Quorum requirement in the by-laws and committee mandates

evidence.note: Typical secretariat logistics; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Prepare answers to directors' questions
steps.description: The sponsoring executive's team prepares short written answers or an extra slide for questions sent in advance, which the secretary posts to the portal or the presenter covers at the meeting.

evidence.note: Share of meetings with advance questions and times are author estimates.

steps.name: Brief the chair before the meeting
steps.description: The chief executive and the secretary hold a short call with the chair to walk through the agenda, sensitive items, expected decisions and any director concerns raised in advance.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Hold the meeting and take notes
steps.description: The secretary confirms quorum, records conflicts of interest declared by directors, and notes the discussion, motions, votes, decisions, conditions and actions while management presents. Regular meetings run about two to four hours.

error.defect_description: A decision, condition or action is noted ambiguously.

control.basis: The model manager Act, 2015 s. 6(2) applying Business Corporations Act s. 132: directors disclose material interests in writing or have them entered in the minutes

evidence.note: The conflict disclosure rule and its application to the model manager are stated; meeting length of two to four hours is published guidance.

steps.name: Directors meet in camera without management
steps.description: At the end of the meeting directors meet without management, and sometimes without the secretary; the chair later tells the chief executive of any resulting actions.

evidence.note: Peer board committees meet without management; frequency at the model manager is an author assumption.

steps.name: Draft the minutes and resolutions
steps.description: The secretary writes the minutes from the notes in the house style: attendance and quorum, conflicts declared, decisions with resolution text, and actions with owners and dates.

error.defect_description: A resolution or action is worded differently from what was decided.

evidence.note: Minutes record decisions, votes and recusals; times are author estimates.

steps.name: General counsel reviews the draft minutes
steps.description: The general counsel checks the draft minutes for legal accuracy, especially the wording of resolutions, delegations of authority and conflict of interest entries, and returns comments to the secretary.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Chair reviews the draft minutes
steps.description: The draft goes to the chair, who reads it and sends changes. The minutes are then circulated to directors and approved formally at the next meeting.

control.basis: Minutes reviewed by the chair and approved at the next meeting

evidence.note: Draft to the chair as soon as practicable, then circulation and approval at the next meeting; wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Update the action log and send decisions to owners
steps.description: The secretary records each action with owner and due date, sends resolution extracts to the teams whose work they start (pool launches, plans, audits, compensation, strategy) and adds approval of these minutes to the next meeting's agenda.

error.defect_description: An action is not assigned or its owner is not told.

evidence.note: Decisions confirmed promptly after the meeting; times are author estimates.

steps.name: File records and update governance registers
steps.description: The coordinator files the draft minutes and certified resolutions, archives the book in the portal, updates the attendance register used in the annual report and sends certified copies to counterparties or the custodian when a resolution is needed for their records.

control.basis: Corporate records kept under the by-laws; director attendance disclosed in the annual report

evidence.note: Director attendance by meeting is published in the annual report; times are author estimates.

steps.name: Call a special meeting at short notice
steps.description: For an urgent decision, such as a large investment with a seller deadline or a market crisis, the secretary agrees the need with the chief executive and chair, polls directors for a slot within days, issues notice and asks the sponsor for a single focused paper.

evidence.note: Boards held extra and special meetings in 2020 and for specific approvals; share of special meetings is an author estimate.

steps.name: Circulate the short-notice paper and confirm attendance
steps.description: The coordinator loads the single paper to the portal as soon as the sponsor and chief executive approve it, confirms quorum and sets up the video call. Directors get one to three days to read.

error.defect_description: Paper circulated without full supporting analysis.

evidence.note: Short-notice timings are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Papers returned for rework
exceptions.description: The secretary, general counsel, chief risk officer or chief executive sends one or more papers back to the sponsor for a clearer decision request, shorter length or corrected numbers.

exceptions.name: Late paper or addendum after publication
exceptions.description: A paper arrives after the book is published, usually because source data closed late or a deal moved, and the book is republished with less reading time.

exceptions.name: Special meeting at short notice
exceptions.description: An urgent investment approval or a market event needs a decision before the next scheduled meeting; one paper is circulated with one to three days' notice.

exceptions.name: Chair or counsel changes the minutes
exceptions.description: The general counsel or chair changes the wording of a resolution or action, sending the draft back to the secretary.

exceptions.name: Decision deferred
exceptions.description: Directors ask for more analysis and defer a decision to the next meeting; the item is carried forward on the action log and the paper comes back in the next cycle.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from opening the meeting file to filing the chair-reviewed minutes
benchmarks.population: Regular and special board and committee meetings at a Canadian public-sector asset manager

evidence.note: Author estimate: preparation starts six to seven weeks ahead so papers can be published a week before the meeting, and minutes take two to three weeks to clear the general counsel and chair.

benchmarks.population: The model manager board and its committees

evidence.note: Counts stated in the 2020, 2021 and 2022 annual reports.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days before the meeting (recommended minimum)

evidence.note: Published guidance recommends at least one week.

benchmarks.population: Corporate directors interviewed by Korn Ferry

evidence.note: Range reported by directors; not specific to public-sector asset managers.

pain_points.description: Papers arrive late or long because they depend on other processes closing (audits, performance, valuations), leaving directors little reading time and forcing republication.

evidence.note: Directors report packs of hundreds of pages arriving a few days before meetings.

pain_points.description: Agenda setting and sign-off wait on the chief executive's and the chair's calendars, which sets the pace more than the work itself.

evidence.note: Author judgement from the step structure.

pain_points.description: Several reviewers (secretary, general counsel, chief risk officer, chief executive) each send papers back, so a paper can be rewritten two or three times.

evidence.note: Author judgement; rework shares are estimates.

pain_points.description: Minutes take weeks to clear the general counsel and the chair, so actions reach owners late.

evidence.note: Guidance asks for drafts to go to the chair as soon as practicable, which implies delay is common.

assumptions: Unit of work is one meeting of the board or one of its committees; each case runs from opening the file about six to seven weeks ahead to filing the chair-reviewed minutes. Formal approval of the minutes is an agenda item of the next meeting.

The organisation file lists audit, investment, risk, human resources and governance committees; the annual reports show four committees in 2021 (finance and audit, human resources and compensation, nominating and governance, and a Board Investment Committee of all directors from 23 September 2021) and no separate risk committee. Volume follows the annual reports (about 2.3 a month).

Executive sponsors' paper work is represented by the cfo role at the sponsor-review level only; the analysis inside each paper belongs to the upstream processes that trigger this one. Attendance of executives at meetings is not counted as hands-on time.
The in-camera session is assumed at every meeting, following peer practice; the share of special meetings (12%) reflects the extra meetings of 2020 and short-notice investment approvals.

No public source gives the model manager's paper deadlines, portal or review rules; steps, times and rework shares are author estimates checked against published guidance on board materials and minutes.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's ranges. Roles with no wage source opened (board secretariat, executive assistant, executives) carry tier C evidence.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: 10 board, 6 finance and audit, 6 human resources and compensation, 4 nominating and governance meetings and 2 Board Investment Committee meetings in 2021; nine directors; Board Investment Committee of all directors created 23 September 2021 to approve investment decisions and review asset allocation advice; four board committees and their mandates; annual board evaluation; Management Investment Committee co-chaired by the CIO and chief risk officer with the general counsel and other senior managers, which must first recommend every investment decision needing board approval; three Investment Department Committees (Total Portfolio, Equities and Credit, Real Assets) set up in 2021 that approve up to thresholds; Investment Approval Policy; one benchmark per asset class investment policy statement; benchmark policy (Risk researches and reviews, Management Investment Committee recommends, board approves); liquidity coverage ratio of high-quality liquid assets to stressed net outflows including client outflows, rebalancing, capital calls and foreign exchange hedging, under past stresses and a one-in-20-year event; counterparty exposure measured daily with ISDA netting and collateral; clean SOC 1 Type I report on control design. sources.supports: 5 board, 7 Board Investment Committee, 6 finance and audit, 4 human resources and compensation and 5 nominating and governance meetings in 2022; board meets at least quarterly; Management Investment Committee composition and delegation to Investment Department Committees; benchmark policy; leverage used for the first time in 2022 at the total portfolio level and a leverage framework and guideline setting client targets and pool-level limits; new risk and total portfolio management system partly live December 2022; systematic rebalancing; currency hedging named as a useful tool; liquidity coverage ratio definition; expanded liquidity analysis in 2022. sources.title: Endowment Governance Part 3: Process and Engagement
sources.supports: Chair owns the agenda with staff; materials at least a week before the meeting; regular meetings of two to four hours; record attendance, votes by name and recusals; circulate minutes promptly to confirm decisions; members should vote on asset allocation, benchmark and risk parameter changes.

sources.title: 10 Tips for Corporate Board Materials: The Year in Governance
sources.publisher: American Bar Association, Business Law Today
sources.supports: Distributing board materials at least one week before meetings is consistent with best practice; use executive summaries; avoid excessive or repetitive material; management confirms accuracy.

sources.title: Board materials due for a makeover
sources.supports: Directors report pre-meeting packages of about 200 to more than 950 pages, typically received a few days before the meeting; 36% of surveyed directors raised concerns about the quality and quantity of materials.

sources.title: Why board minutes matter
sources.supports: Draft minutes go to the chair as soon as practicable, the chair reviews and circulates them, directors respond promptly, and the board approves them at the next meeting; signed minutes are not amended.

sources.title: Publishing a book (Boards help, Diligent One Platform)
sources.supports: Administrators build the book, review it as a director would see it, publish it, keep editing after publication and republish so late additions appear; unapproved documents do not show.

sources.title: The Directors' Briefing: Conflicts of Interest by Officers
sources.supports: Ontario Business Corporations Act s. 132(1): a director or officer with a material interest in a material contract or transaction shall disclose it in writing or request to have it entered in the minutes of directors' meetings.

sources.title: The model manager Act, 2015, S.O. 2015, c. 20, Sched. 19 (sections 1 to 12)
sources.supports: s. 6(2) applies Business Corporations Act s. 132 (conflict of interest) and s. 136 (indemnification) to the model manager; s. 9 members sign an investment management agreement; s. 10 annual meeting within 15 months of the previous one; s. 12 board of seven to 11 directors, six to eight elected and one to three appointed by the Minister, all independent.

sources.title: The national pension fund manager F2021 Annual Report (fiscal year ended March 31, 2021)
sources.supports: Peer practice: nine regular board meetings plus five committees meeting six to eight times and special meetings; audit committee meets auditors without management; CEO sets Investment Management Authorities with transaction approval limits for an Investment Decision Committee and department committees, and the board's investment committee approves transactions above set amounts.
